pages.title: Farther Away
pages.text: $(bold)Warning:$() If this experiment fails, there may be nothing left nearby. I will not build the reactor near a base, valuable terrain, or another reactor; the farther away, the better.$(br2)The Core, Stabilizers, Injector, and power system must be kept together, and no part of them can stop while the reactor is running. The containment field also needs its own backup power supply.

pages.title: Six Axes Only
pages.text: I tried moving a Stabilizer slightly aside, but the Core refused to recognize it. Stabilizers and Energy Injectors apparently must lie on the six cardinal axes, 4–7 blocks away, facing the Core with nothing but air between them.$(br2)The easiest arrangement to inspect places four Stabilizers on the horizontal plane and reserves the vertical axis for the Energy Injector. At least this makes incorrect connections less likely.

pages.name: Four Stabilizers
pages.text: This trial uses the minimum distance of four blocks. All four Stabilizers face inward. Purple only marks the Core's position; the actual Reactor Core belongs there.

pages.name: Top Injector
pages.text: With the horizontal plane occupied by Stabilizers, the Energy Injector has to sit 4–7 blocks directly above the Core, facing downward, with containment energy supplied from its outer side. A second Injector can also be placed below the Core. The entire arrangement should rotate together.

pages.title: Core and Stabilizers
pages.text: Both the Reactor Core and its Stabilizers require late-stage Fusion Crafting. One reactor uses exactly one Core and four Stabilizers. It is best to prepare all five before leaving; there is no reason to run back for one missing part.

pages.title: Containment Lifeline
pages.text: The Energy Injector also requires Fusion Crafting. One is enough to operate the reactor, though another may be added on the opposite side. Keep at least one spare far from the reactor site. If anything happens, a spare left nearby will only disappear with everything else.
